text.p: French glassmaker Saint-Gobain SA said on Thursday its 1996 net attributable profit would be 4.32 billion francs ($780.3 million), up slightly from last year.

The company said the provisional result proved "the solidity of the group in a poor European economic environment, especially in the building sector, that is compensated by sustained activity on the American continent."
It said the profit was booked after 1.2 billion francs in restructuring charges.

Chairman Jean-Louis Beffa said in a telephone interview that the 1997 result would show good progress due to the asset gain on the sale of a majority stake in contract management firm Cise to a subsidiary of building company Bouygues for 2.16 billion francs.
He declined to give a prediction for pre-exceptional results, saying it was too early to do so.
Beffa said the restructuring charges, more than double the 569 million francs of provisions set aside in 1995, showed the company's willingness to tackle its problems. ($1=5.536 French Franc)
